title: Ovulation Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Ovulation Calculator: Fertile window and ovulation date. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Fertile window and ovulation date. Enter your first day of last period and cycle length and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before your next period. You're most fertile in the five days before ovulation and on the day itself. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Pregnancy tools include [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator), [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) and [Pregnancy Weight Gain Calculator](/pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator).

## How to use the Ovulation Calculator

Start by picking your first day of last period, then entering your cycle length (days). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Pick your first day of last period.
2. Enter your cycle length (days).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Ovulation ≈ LMP + (cycle length − 14). Fertile window = ovulation − 5 days to ovulation + 1 day.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## What the result shows

With the default values (First day of last period: 2026-03-01, Cycle length: 28 days), the [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) returns Estimated ovulation: Sun, March 15, 2026, Fertile window starts: Tue, March 10, 2026, Fertile window ends: Mon, March 16, 2026, Next period: Sun, March 29, 2026. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Ovulation test kits detect the LH surge 24–36 hours before ovulation.
- Track basal body temperature to confirm patterns.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use this as contraception?

No. Cycles vary, so calendar estimates are not reliable birth control. Try it with your own numbers in the [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How long does an egg live?

About 12–24 hours after ovulation, while sperm can survive up to 5 days. Try it with your own numbers in the [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Ovulation Calculator use?

Ovulation ≈ LMP + (cycle length − 14). Fertile window = ovulation − 5 days to ovulation + 1 day. You can see it in action in the [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Ovulation Calculator?

Just First day of last period and Cycle length. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
